summary: CI-only change. Every cached jdx/mise-action step in 12 workflows (29 steps) gains a cache_key_prefix naming its job's runner image (mise-v1-ubuntu-2204 or mise-v1-ubuntu-2404), so ubuntu-22.04 and ubuntu-24.04 jobs stop sharing a mise cache entry that holds glibc-specific cargo-built tools. A new vitest guard (scripts/__tests__/workflow-mise-cache-image.test.mjs) enforces the prefix/runs-on pairing. No library, SQL, payload or release workflow behaviour changes; no shipped artefact is affected. A re-implementation of the guard's check over the head tree found every cached step's prefix matches its runs-on image and both composite actions cache only wasm-pack. Residual risks are CI-only: whether the older v3.6.3 pin honours cache_key_prefix (could not be verified offline), and a one-time cold cache on every job. Impact low; ready for normal review.

behaviour_changes.description: Cached mise-action steps now write and restore cache entries under an image-specific prefix (mise-v1-ubuntu-2204 / mise-v1-ubuntu-2404) instead of the action's default prefix, so jobs on different Ubuntu images no longer share a key. All existing mise cache entries for these steps stop being hit; the first run of each job after merge reinstalls tools.

New discovery test asserts every cached mise-action step in .github/workflows sets cache_key_prefix = mise-v1-<image of runs-on>, sets no cache_key, turns the cache off when runs-on names no image, and that composite actions cache only image-independent tools. Runs in tests.yml via `pnpm run test:scripts` on every PR.

failure_scenarios.title: cache_key_prefix silently ignored on the v3.6.3 mise-action pin
failure_scenarios.trigger: The pinned jdx/mise-action@5228313 (v3.6.3) used by tests-rust.yml and integration-protect-ffi.yml does not accept or does not use cache_key_prefix in its key.
failure_scenarios.mechanism: GitHub Actions only warns on an unknown `with:` input. Two cached steps use the older v3.6.3 pin rather than v4 (1648a78). If that version ignores the input, those 2404 jobs keep the default, image-blind key, while the guard test still passes because it checks only the YAML.
failure_scenarios.consequence: The original GLIBC mismatch could persist for any job still on the shared default key; with 2204 jobs moved off it, the remaining sharers are only these two 2404 jobs, so the practical effect is small. CI-only, no shipped artefact.

existing_verification.description: Guard test checks the YAML input is present, not that the action honours it

missing_verification: Confirm from the v3.6.3 action.yml (or a CI log's cache key line) that cache_key_prefix is a supported input that feeds the key
failure_scenarios.mitigation: Check one CI run's 'Cache saved with key' line for tests-rust / integration-protect-ffi; or bump those pins to the v4 sha used elsewhere.

failure_scenarios.title: One-time cold mise cache on every affected job
failure_scenarios.trigger: First run of each job after merge.
failure_scenarios.mechanism: New prefixes miss all existing entries, so mise reinstalls tools, including compiling cargo: tools (cargo-nextest, cargo-llvm-cov, cargo-mutants, cargo-udeps, cargo-fuzz) from source.
failure_scenarios.consequence: Slower first runs and more registry downloads; a transient upstream fetch failure would fail a job that previously hit cache. Loud and self-healing.
failure_scenarios.mitigation: None needed beyond accepting slower first runs; re-run on transient fetch failure.
